cells.tense: What you tended is bearing fruit and you are standing in it now.
cells.act: release the method, not the purpose
cells.ask: Take a project you're finishing — a room, a stretch of a relationship, a piece of work — and stop improving how you're doing it. Keep the point. Drop the better way. Let the work be done as it is.
cells.core:
What you've been building toward is here — abundant enough that you can stand in it instead of pushing it further. You can point your energy at what you want and mean it, and at this size that's the whole gift. Something you tended for a long time is paying off, and you get to decide what happens next, not just keep tending.

When a way of doing it has run its course, let that go and keep the purpose. The release comes easy when the work is complete; it isn't the same as quitting. What's left after the method goes is the reason you started, and that reason is what you're free to feed next. Feed the purpose. The method can rest.
cells.sheetLine: You can choose your direction instead of only finishing it.
cells.verb: Bearing what the days added up to, and trusting it holds
cells.place: Where direction gets chosen and held

cells.tense: You will push the garden to produce before it has finished growing.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Bring one other person into a job you're steering alone. Not to hand it over — their pace sets half of it, yours the other half. Run it that way a while.
cells.core:
The harvest is coming in and you're trying to have it all now — checking whether it's enough before it's grown, steering toward a picture you can already see and can't stop revising. What was care has tightened into control, and the tighter hold is what's making it feel like it might not arrive at all.

Let one other person into the direction-setting. If two people share the same aim, you stop having to hold the whole thing by yourself, and the promise you're bracing against can actually be met by hands other than yours. You're not giving up the steering. You're letting someone steer beside you, and finding out the thing you built is strong enough to hold two sets of hands. That is what the work was for.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing for the result instead of letting it arrive.
cells.verb: Bearing what the days added up to, and trusting it holds
cells.place: Where direction gets chosen and held

cells.tense: You stood at the door of your own direction and never crossed it.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Name a heading you actually want — not the one you'd be expected to want. Then take a step this week that only makes sense if that's where you're going.
cells.core:
There's a harvest you didn't collect. Something you tended came in, and the spending of it got left behind. You're pointed at what was, not what's here. It isn't laziness. The fuel for wanting ran low, so you stopped surveying and stopped asking what you'd like to see.

One point of light is enough to move toward. Decide it from what you want, not from the reasoning, and take one step that fits the choice. You don't have to feel ready. The energy comes back through the going, not before it. Three days of one heading beats a year of checking every signpost, and a small true step is what starts the movement again.
cells.sheetLine: What you wanted grew up and you left it behind.
cells.verb: Bearing what the days added up to, and trusting it holds
cells.place: Where direction gets chosen and held

cells.tense: You are steering something right now without noticing you chose it.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Notice what you're steering toward this month, then go at the hardest solid part of it on purpose — one session, no dodging the friction. See what holds when you push.
cells.core:
The choice runs so far back you stopped seeing yourself do it. The direction was set long before and you keep it going — the tending, the aiming, the saying this not that — and you'd tell it as just how things are. The decision did happen. It's still happening. The people on the other end of it can see the hand on the wheel.

Take the hard part head-on. When you push against the resistance on purpose, you find out whether the aim is yours or whether it was running you. The friction shows what's solid. What holds under the push is what you actually meant, and finding that out is how the steering comes back into your own hands, where it has been the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: You chose this direction and forgot that you chose it.
cells.verb: Bearing what the days added up to, and trusting it holds
cells.place: Where direction gets chosen and held
